newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA TO ALLOW PRIVATE OIL REFINERIES.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA TO ALLOW PRIVATE OIL REFINERIES.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto has issued a decree allowing private firms to build oil refineries on their own or jointly with state oil company Pertamina.

"In an effort to maintain national developement and to strengthen the economy...in refining and processing crude oil and gas, new refineries are needed in order to fulfil domestic needs," he said in a presidential decree dated July 31. A copy of the document was obtained by Reuters on Monday.
"Private companies can cooperate with Pertamina in building and operating the refineries through part capital ownership," he said in the decree.
The decree said private refineries can be set up by Indonesian companies or in partership with foreign firms.
It said Pertamina will remain the sole distributor of fuel products in the domestic market, but added that fuel products not needed by Pertamina can be exported by private refineries.
The decree said Pertamina will enter into long-term contracts to buy fuel products from private refineries at prices quoted in the international market.
Indonesia's Pertamina has long encourage private sector to build new refineries, but without any luck because of a lack of proper guidelines. Suharto's decree is expected to overcome that problem.
Pertamina currently operates eight refineries, with a combined capacity of 989,500 barrels per day.
